sanskrit_verse:
ततश् चानेन मन्त्रेण सकृत् तद् अभिमन्त्रयेत् ।
परं पवित्रम् अमृतं घृत त्वं यज्ञकर्मसु ॥
transliteration:
tataś cānena mantreṇa sakṛt tad abhimantrayet |
paraṃ pavitram amṛtaṃ ghṛta tvaṃ yajñakarmasu ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Thereafter, with this mantra once invoked, that which is supremely pure, immortal, and clarified butter shall be consecrated for sacrificial acts.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the sanctity of invocation
Causation flows from conscious intent in ritual action
Capacity-based responsibility lies in proper consecration
Restoration logic aligns through purified offerings
Consciousness alignment occurs via sacred utterance
executable_legal_axioms: IF an offering is made THEN it must be first invoked by prescribed mantra
IF a substance is used in sacrifice THEN it becomes purified by declaration
IF a ritual act commences THEN all elements involved are elevated to divine status
IF consciousness aligns with mantra THEN material causality transforms accordingly
supreme_court_application: In matters concerning ceremonial law or constitutional validity of religious practices, invocation through recognized mantras establishes jurisdictional purity. The court must recognize that properly consecrated substances carry inherent legal sanctity within Vedic jurisprudence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa arises from correct recitation; anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as transformation of ghee into amṛtam through sound. Responsibility rests on accurate pronunciation, not punitive oversight. Outcome reflects correctness of cause, not imposition of consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Re-invocation until correct resonance achieved
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Priest reaffirms alignment with source sound
Capacity Restoration: Reciter undergoes purification before repetition
Integrity Reintegration: Substance is re-consecrated under supervision
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this verse upholds Dharma through precise ritual execution. No punishment arises where error stems from lack of capacity—only completion restores alignment. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
